negative_constraints: **Search-in-thread highlights (24.4.3) -- full spec (MVP):** (1) **Purpose:** When user searches in thread (§10), highlight matching text in visible messages; only visible items need highlight computation. (2) **When:** Thread view focused after search; optional "Highlight all in thread" mode while scrolling until search cleared. (3) **UI:** Distinct highlight style (e.g. background or underline), consistent across types/themes; only visible window scanned; cache match ranges per message ID so re-entering visible window restores highlights; highlight all occurrences; optional Next/Previous match (keyboard). (4) **Data:** Store match ranges (start, end offset) per message; compute on search or when message enters view; cache by (message_id, query); thread search query available to chat view; clear on search clear or thread change. (5) **Performance:** Do not re-scan full thread on scroll--cache ranges for all matching messages at search time, or compute only for visible slice and cache by message ID. (6) **Edge cases:** Cap matches per message (e.g. 50); escape regex/special chars; empty query = no highlights.

Version 1 readers reject unknown payload fields/versions. Any successor schema or withdrawal needs owner migration and a separately reviewed registry revision; malformed or unknown-family inputs follow Storage quarantine rules without checkpoint advance. An otherwise valid unsupported future-version record remains untouched; the consumer halts with `unsupported_schema_version` and preserves its last supported sequence until a compatible reader is available. owner_consumer: ## External Research Decision Packet Consumer Addendum (2026-09-17)

External research packets (`Plans/External_Research.md`, `ERS-005`) are delivered through the decision flow this owner already defines under `DL-036`: one chat artifact holding every item, then one item at a time as a plain-language card answered with exactly one of Approve, Deny, Deny with changes, or Ask a question, with the full artifact openable throughout and status shown in text labels. Nothing about that surface changes for research packets. What this addendum records is the consumer boundary: the research owner supplies the packet content and the finding reference behind each item, and this owner keeps the artifact, the card, the response set, the questionnaire reuse and the presentation rules. A research finding classed `correction` never becomes a card, because corrections land under the standing repair authorization without a user decision; only `capability` and `product_choice` items reach this surface.

heading_text: Grill Me rounds and agreement — DL-218

owner_consumer: The session ends by itself only when no decision is ready, no fact research is pending and no branch is unsettled. A decision left open, and every decision that depends on it, is listed as open in What we agreed and does not count as an unsettled branch. If every remaining question waits on research, the host waits, says it is looking things up and recomputes when research returns. Automatic completion, the safety cap and Wrap up each show that session's What we agreed card with every answer and every open decision and reason. It is a review of existing answers, not a new charged QuestionItem. Wrap up uses cmd.questionnaire.grill_me.wrap_up and preserves any unfinished draft without submitting it. Confirm uses cmd.questionnaire.grill_me.confirm against the current agreement revision; only its acknowledged owner result confirms the accumulated decisions. Keep going uses cmd.questionnaire.grill_me.keep_going to return to the same interview with its answers and one counter intact. At the cap it may revisit existing answers but cannot admit another fresh question. Each newly presented question is still charged once under QMAX; a recommendation, action button or agreement render charges nothing.

The three typed request/result pairs live in Plans/assistant_chat_contracts.schema.json and its fixture pair. They reference the existing host session and source flow, current questionnaire and agreement, revision and currentness; they define no new durable record family. The session states interviewing, awaiting_confirmation and confirmed describe this profile's owner state, not new QuestionnaireEnvelope.flow_state values. The envelope's answer sources, response_kind and lifecycle enums stay locked. Authenticated host user provenance, revision checks and idempotent replay apply; an actor_ref string supplied by an agent is never proof of user action. Dismissal still pauses, resume restores the same paused envelope, and neither confirms or wraps up. No step may consume the staged agreement before that session's current Confirm. Initially this gates Plan writes, Crew split, room round 1 or BrainStorm blind proposals. Enabling Grill Me mid-run starts the interview at the next round, assignment or phase boundary; already running work continues, and only the step using new answers waits. Every later decision session ends in its own What we agreed revision with fresh Confirm and the same question counter. A stale confirmation changes nothing. The controls never mutate a target project, start execution or grant permission. No EventRecord is admitted (DL-093).

owner_consumer: **Catch-up.** `catch_up_seconds` is `0|15|30|60` with default `30`. A catch-up wait is a bounded delay of the primary at a configured frozen boundary, or when a `critical` held finding exists, so the advisor can converge. It is never a hard interrupt and never an abort. The wait is user-abortable, shows an honest notice naming why it is waiting, releases immediately when the advisor converges, and releases when the cap expires. There is no ordinary background catch-up delay when no critical held advice exists. `0` means the primary never waits.

**Cooldown.** After an emitted `concern` or `critical` steer, `interruption_cooldown_turns` (default `3`) primary turns pass before another interrupting-severity emission is routed the same way. During cooldown, later concerns are routed as non-interrupting asides at the next step boundary rather than being dropped, and `nit` routing is unchanged. Cooldown never discards a finding; it changes only its delivery channel and timing.

Project Registry owns archive; its acknowledged owner consequence consumes the shared project_archive_backup_child_result_v1 and carries exact Project/policy revision, archive transition/occurrence fence and idempotent pause result. Failure or unreachable scheduler is shown as an incomplete pause, never silently certified. Archive admits no prune/delete and does not stop an already captured run by UI inference. Unarchive rechecks current Backup policy, scheduler/Stop/eligibility and missed-run rules; it never silently starts a backup, clears a stop or bursts a backlog. Explicit Back Up Now remains separately available subject to normal owner admission.

Full Server Backup includes canonical app chats/history, scratch notebook, Goals/GoalRuns/control/history, Crew/coordination/boards, Assistant Plans/Deep Plan ledgers/bundles/PlanRuns/adherence, scheduled messages/tasks/windows/consents/occurrences and app Stop/pause custody admitted by their owners. Visible No project chat folders are included by default as optional source families; exclusion and unreachable content are recorded in the manifest and never called complete. Store capture keeps DL-270 brief barrier/coherence, one writer, source retention/holds and the same counterpart caps. Derived indexes/caches rebuild and never replace canonical bodies or accepted sources. Settings-level records follow their admitted server/home custody; backup does not transfer operational authority or credentials.

After chat conversion, Project Backup includes the full destination-owned copied conversation, destination notebook and linked new Goal/Plan/Crew records and explicitly re-admitted destination schedules. Optional association rebind remains unavailable until its separate complete owner protocol is admitted. Original app event/body/approval bytes remain at original scope and sealed source custody according to ACD-511/N25; an app copy expiring after Undo never purges independently retained canonical task/body/audit or shared payload anchors. Restoring old app chat/history compares the current conversion lineage/tombstone/cutover generation before activation, preventing two live copies or old schedules firing again. A restore may retain historical content without admitting a second writer or source continuation. Cross-Server transfer requires current owner evidence, not a string path.

Restore as New rewrites PM-internal identities/references only. External forge host/account/repository identity remains non-authoritative lineage until explicit Source Control/Forge rebind and current remote validation. Restored credential refs, approvals, execution leases, schedules, Stop state and provider routes do not auto-authorize or resume work; original owner recovery/activation rules govern. Project archive/rename/remove and conversion Undo never delete a remote repository, branch, external backup or modified work.

Full Server Backup includes the settings-home Everywhere values/history and their admitted home metadata. Project Backup/restore covers only Project own values and destination records and cannot replace Everywhere or elect a settings home; any home replacement is an explicit protected owner restore. BuildGrant, CreatedResourceManifest, grant/Stop/revocation and action/recovery evidence are retained canonical build history under their admitted Project scope and coherent backup graph, not disposable projections. A restored grant is historical evidence, never resurrected authority, and the existing original phase-custody rules including BRS-029 remain exact. Where no safe inverse exists, the owner action report says No safe Undo.

WN-021 and AMS-054 also enroll canonical application-thread notebook checkpoints and memory/gist/teaching records in coherent Full Server Backup where their owner retention policy requires them. Thread-only isolation, verification/source restrictions, independent holds and public_safe rule ownership remain intact; derived indexes/caches are not replacement custody and these bodies never enter Settings copy or a Starter.

The CV-366/367 and SP-349/350/351/352/353 source contracts require the coherent Full Server Backup manifest to retain the actual canonical app Goal body/history/origin/control/receipt/association sources; Crew definitions/runs/transcripts/board/coordination; Assistant Plan exact revisions/ledger/bundle/PlanRun/adherence and To-Dos; scheduled-message/window/consent/correlation/occurrence/pause/Stop sources and durable timer dedupe; and scratch notebook/checkpoint/payload/restriction custody. Include chat folders is optional and on by default. Project Backup includes the full converted conversation and destination-owned canonical records, while independently retained app task/audit sources and holds follow their actual owner lifetimes after Undo expires. The CV-366/367 and SP-349/350/351/352/353 source/retention graph, including required permission/build evidence, is mandatory; missing durable root, policy or authentic source is a typed unavailable/incomplete capture, never inferred completeness from a receipt or cache.

Before restored content becomes live or any timer is admitted, the owner checks current thread lineage, cutover generation, source and target writer, deletion/tombstone, holds, user_stop_epoch and app/Project/per-task pause/Stop. An old app backup cannot undo a current deletion, clear a newer Stop/pause, revive source continuation, produce a second live chat/run or dispatch an occurrence twice. Retaining historical evidence does not activate it. Protected restore, Recovery Kit and original BRS-029 source/cancellation custody remain exact; derived events/projections cannot reconstruct missing accepted source or authority.

Because OpenAI, Anthropic, MiniMax, Gemini, and Bedrock can format tool calls differently across JSON shape, parallel-tool layout, provider call identifiers, finish metadata, schema subsets, or stream framing, provider adapters MUST preserve those provider/runtime facts through parsing, sanitization, and payload preflight before normalizing them into PM's canonical tool-call event stream.

For JSON, JSONL, and `/NDJSON` streams from LLM providers, including GLM-4.7, GLM-5, and Kimi, parser state is incremental and chunk-boundary aware. A bridge accumulates partial UTF-8 and line-delimited fragments until a complete JSON value is available; malformed or incomplete fragments become structured provider error events and never become fabricated tool calls, silently dropped history, or reserialized clean output.

Stream resilience is a facade-level floor, with provider-specific constants allowed only when they preserve the shared retry taxonomy. Reconnect/resume attempts are bounded to `max_retries=3` unless a stricter provider policy applies, use exponential backoff `1s -> 2s -> 4s` with `+/-25%` jitter, and open a circuit breaker after `5` consecutive transient stream failures within `2 minutes`; the breaker stays open for `30s`, then moves through half-open probe state before close/reopen. `Plans/Provider_OpenCode.md` (`/Provider_OpenCode.md`) records the OpenCode-specific streaming-resilience owner details, but those details must remain compatible with this facade floor.

owner_consumer: ## 14. Settings boundary

Settings stores ordinary defaults at their exact inventory-admitted Everywhere/Computer/Project levels and renders the manager; app reads omit Project. This owner stores committed definitions/runs/frozen rosters. Settings never stores transcripts, assignments, findings, votes or question banks; this owner is never a second default-value writer.

These keys require Settings inventory census and registration through `Plans/Settings_System.md` and `Plans/settings_inventory.json`; they are named here to fix the ownership boundary, not to claim registration. A default read at modal-open time is a snapshot: changing a Settings default afterward never retroactively alters a committed definition or a running run. The effective roster frozen at start is the run's truth, and the panel shows it even after Settings change.

owner_consumer: ## 16. Provider boundary and control

Puppet Master owns the canonical collaborative state across direct, SDK, CLI, and server providers. A provider adapter may translate a Puppet Master participant request into a provider request and a provider event into a normalized Puppet Master event. Translation never transfers authority.

Provider-native multi-agent, sub-session, or team constructs are not the canonical run. Where a provider exposes one, it is disabled, redirected into the canonical run, or marked noncanonical, and its state is never read back as Puppet Master truth. Participant tools, MCP servers, skills, permissions, and artifacts remain owned by `Plans/Tools.md`, `Plans/MCP_Integration.md`, `Plans/Skills_System.md`, `Plans/Permissions_System.md`, and the artifact owners respectively.

compatibility_only: Project-focused Kubernetes linkage keeps deploy and troubleshoot work in Docker Manager without turning Puppet Master into a general cluster admin console, cloud-provider console, or cluster-administration UX. The conditional `Kubernetes` subview preserves kubeconfig/context, namespace, `/namespace/workload` focus, log viewer defaults, auto-refresh and `/watch` toggles, Helm visibility, Helm release focus, persisted K8s focus state, and a `cluster-wide` resources toggle defaulted off. Command coverage is `cmd.docker.k8s.apply/diff/logs/exec/port_forward/select_context/select_namespace`, `cmd.docker.k8s.apply|diff|logs|exec|port_forward|set_context|set_namespace|helm_preview|helm_install`, `/logs/exec/port-forward/Helm/workload`, including the explicit command `cmd.docker.k8s.apply`; compatibility aliases from older `cmd.k8s.*` rows normalize to this Docker Manager namespace. Deploy, `/rollout/apply`, `/apply/rollout`, log, exec, `port_forward`, Helm, and `/troubleshoot` failures open directly to project-relevant workload status, logs, or diff. If `kubectl`, kubeconfig, or cluster access is missing, the subview remains visible with setup guidance and explicit `/connection` state instead of disappearing. Docker Manager's Kubernetes view defaults to the project-focused subset; full cluster inventory requires the explicit `cluster-wide` toggle and remains visually distinct from project scope. `/attempt/action` receipts are `collapse-by-default`; over-verbose logs stay behind detail expansion. `/tradeoffs`: visibility must stay project-centered, cluster-facing explorer scope must be intentionally constrained to project-relevant resources, and cluster-wide views default off.

Operation receipts are the compact auditable record for important side effects across Orchestrator history/detail, Source Control commit/push, GitHub Actions run panes, Docker publish panes, registry promotion, and Kubernetes apply/rollout. They are compact UI objects derived from canonical run/publish/events, not ad hoc strings. compatibility_only: ### 1.3 EventEnvelopeV1 -- minimal compatibility envelope

Projectors normalize this shape in memory for replay only; they never append or rewrite it during ordinary read/replay. The normalizer's inputs are the exact admitted envelope/extensions, the verified seglog header and source cursor, and the registered event-family row containing scope policy, payload schema, and explicit legacy identity JSON pointers. Current time, randomness, filesystem mtime, absolute paths, process identity, hash-map order, UI-selected project, and mutable account/session state are forbidden inputs.

Deterministic normalization uses UTC RFC3339 with exactly nine fractional digits and trailing `Z`, then RFC 8785 canonical JSON over `{ts, seq, type, payload, extensions}`. Let `legacy_digest` be lowercase SHA-256 hex of its UTF-8 bytes. The normalized `event_id` is `legacy-event-v1:{legacy_digest}` and `idempotency_key` is `legacy-envelope-v1:{legacy_digest}`. Canonical MessagePack recursively orders map keys by UTF-8 bytes, uses shortest valid integer/length encodings and UTF-8 strings, and forbids NaN/infinity.
| `event_id` | `legacy-event-v1:{legacy_digest}`. |
| `event_type` | Exact legacy `type` after a registered compatibility alias; unregistered aliases quarantine. |
| `actor_ref` | Registered non-secret actor ref or reserved `pm.actor_ref/legacy-unknown`. |
| `occurred_at_utc` | Canonicalized legacy `ts`; invalid/ambiguous time quarantines. |
| `sequence_id` | Equal verified header sequence when present, otherwise legacy `seq`; disagreement quarantines. |
| `producer_sequence_id` | Null; legacy `seq` is the storage sequence and no upstream sequence is invented. |
| `correlation_id` | Registered ref or `event_id`, making the legacy event its own correlation root. |
| `idempotency_key` | `legacy-envelope-v1:{legacy_digest}`. |
| `payload_schema_id` | Exact registered compatibility schema for normalized event type; missing registration quarantines. |
| `payload` | Legacy payload unchanged after schema and no-secret validation. |
| `payload_ref` | Explicit registered legacy ref or null. |
| `migration.migrated_from_schema_version` | Null because the legacy envelope carried no version. |
| `migration.compatibility_event_type` | Exact original legacy `type` before alias normalization. |

| `request_ref`, `command_id`, `command_instance_id` | Actual normalized request, canonical command and stable command instance; only an unknown pre-dispatch command has null canonical ID, preserving the original input through the request ref. |

heading_text: DL-050: Hosted-repo requests route by the selected adapter, never by default to GitHub

owner_consumer: The question was where the assistant should send a hosted-repository request: to the GitHub command family, as the chat command boundary still said, or to the universal forge commands with the provider taken from the repository the user has selected. It came up because a scoped review of the GitLab plan found the chat boundary still routing every pull request, review, comment, release, pipeline, workflow and hosted-administration request to GitHub, after the wiring rows and the command catalog had already moved to one command per user action with provider differences held in the adapter. A user working on a GitLab project would have had the assistant name and dispatch the wrong service.

1. Route hosted-repository requests to the universal forge command families and resolve the provider from the selected repository adapter, keeping provider-specific families only where the forge owner defines no generic equivalent.
2. Leave the chat boundary pointing at GitHub and add a separate exception for each other provider as it ships.

The answer is option 1. Hosted-repo requests route by the selected adapter and never default to GitHub. Naming a provider, or typing a provider prefix, qualifies the same universal command instead of selecting a different family; the assistant says which provider it resolved and never quietly substitutes another, and when the named provider is not the selected one it says so and asks or refuses under the disclosure rules already written. The boundary between local Git work and hosted work does not move: the assistant still never reinterprets one as the other, a request that spans both still shows the handoff, and the repository, worktree and compare identity still travel between the two stages. Review wording follows the selected adapter's own review noun, so the same request reads as Pull Request or Merge Request without becoming a different command.

Two families stay provider-specific because the forge owner defines no generic equivalent: GitHub Actions, which that owner explicitly keeps GitHub-native inside the shared automation shell, and the GitHub device-code connect and disconnect commands under the same retained owner. Hosted issue work has no registered command family at all, generic or provider-specific, so the assistant says so rather than inventing a command or pushing the request into reviews, pipelines or repository administration.

heading_text: DL-136: A project-wide "Pause all automations" switch stops every scheduled send and build until the user turns it back on (E-19)

owner_consumer: > Superseded in part by DL-292 (2026-11-03). The original Project pause/epoch is unchanged; an independent application/Server pause/epoch now covers app automations through the same operational owner. Earlier ruling text and quoted user words are retained as history.

There is one project-wide switch: "One switch that stops every scheduled send and build until you turn it back on." The design promised that the user's manual pause always wins but showed the switch read-only, and the Plans only paused one run at a time. The switch is a manual stop: turning it on latches a stop at project scope by advancing the `user_stop_epoch` the way Manual Stop does, so every scheduled send and scheduled build in the project fails its dispatch check while it is on. Only the user clears it, by turning it off. No automatic mechanism clears or bypasses it: not a quota reset, a window opening, a schedule time, or a Goal, Plan or Crew continuation, and creating a new schedule while it is on does not clear it either. The command is `cmd.runtime.automation_pause.set`, project-scoped, with the payload `paused` true or false. The card's cost is "A new command and a little runtime work." The card was answered after DL-110 to DL-135 were written, so it takes the next free id. The register lines waiting on this card, B-SQR-05, B-CMD-01 and B-CMD-02, compile it into the owner documents in the WAIT wave; this entry changes no owner text itself.

owner_consumer: > Superseded in part by DL-281 (2026-11-03). MA-073 gains Computer between Everywhere and Project, skipping Project in No project; provider/account owner rungs, exact identity and switch safeguards remain. Earlier ruling text and quoted user words are retained as history.

- Auto-switch, its switch level, its warning level and its rest period after a rate limit can each be set per provider in Settings. A provider without its own value uses the global value, which is the default for all four; the rest period, which until now was set only per account, gains a global value for this. An account's own value still wins over its provider's value, in the order the multi-account spec sets out (made one ladder by the owner decision of 2026-10-10 below).

**Options considered:** For the room's actions: a read-only room with links to Settings, or acting in place; Jared chose acting in place, wired to Settings. For auto-switch: one global policy with a project override, the spec's earlier state, or one policy per provider; Jared chose per provider. The coordinator ruled the details: the provider scope covers the toggle, the switch level, the warning level and the cooldown; the global value is the default for all four, so the cooldown, which had only a per-account value, gains a global one; the Usage card hosts the toggle and the switch level, as the AI Account Center's provider sections do, while all four stay editable in Settings; and the Usage card and Settings edit one value through the Settings owner. These are the coordinator's rulings on Jared's request, not his own answers.

1. **Per-provider auto-switch** (`Plans/Multi-Account.md#MA-073`): the provider scope, the order in which account, provider, project and global values apply, the global value as the default for all four, one value edited by the Usage card and by Settings through the Settings owner, and the switching rules above.

4. **The Accounts room acts in place** (`Plans/usage-feature.md#UF-093`, amended, and `#UF-107`): an account card's body and Details stay a local inspector that dispatches nothing; Use this account and the provider's Auto-switch toggle and switch level are the owner-routed actions carved out of that rule (`Plans/Commands_System.md#CS-067`, amended).

**Owner decision 2026-10-10 (USG-1):** Jared kept the account scope on `ai.accounts.hard-switch-level` and retired `ai.accounts.account-threshold-override`. There is one scope ladder for every threshold, global, then project, then provider, then account, and the most specific set value wins. An account's own switch level is `ai.accounts.hard-switch-level` at scope account; a value stored under the retired id is read once and carried there. The spec now says so in `Plans/Multi-Account.md#MA-073` and section 5, `Plans/Settings_System.md` section 8 and the 2026-10-10 amendment of `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md#F3-441`; the inventory row is marked superseded and kept only for that one carry.

**Owner decision 2026-10-10 (USG-2):** Jared asked for MA-073's status states to be written as a mapping: each state is defined by a set of section 5 reason codes. `Plans/Multi-Account.md` now carries the MA-073 state table, read top to bottom, with no new code and no stored status.

**Owner decision 2026-10-10 (D43):** Jared's words were "account cards get switches", overriding the recommendation to leave an account's own switch level to Settings. Each account card on the Usage page carries one control for `ai.accounts.hard-switch-level` at scope account, on its card and in its Details. Showing it only on the accounts of a provider with two or more accounts is the reading of those words, not part of them: an account whose provider has no other account has nothing to switch to, so its card shows no control, as such a provider shows no auto-switch controls (`Plans/Multi-Account.md#MA-073`). The control is the same value as that account's own row in Settings, not a copy. It shows the level the account resolves to and whether that level is the account's own or follows its provider, and it offers following the provider again, which clears the account's own value. It commits through the same Settings transaction, at scope account with the account id; it keeps the provider's hold rules, so a level at or past the warning level that applies to the account is shown disabled with the reason; and its Open in Settings lands inside that account. The spec now says so in `Plans/Settings_System.md#SSYS-044` and section 8.

owner_consumer: ### DR-054 - One First-Paint Reader Per Page, Reading The Look Owner's Store

A page paints its stored look before its first frame through exactly one first-paint reader (F3-468). The look's one store and the reader's read-only access are DR-056's; this rule adds only the count. The reader writes nothing but the attributes the look owner's first render writes, so the owner rewrites the same values, and no surface on the page adds a reader of its own. The assistant chat keeps its reader (F3-612) only while it is a page of its own; when it is ported into PMConcept7, PMConcept7's head boot script is the page's one reader and the chat's reader is removed rather than kept beside it.

Before a Project opens, the same reader consumes the Settings owner's locally available resolved application/Device look; a valid saved resolution is never replaced with an ephemeral Basic Dark flash. Basic Dark is only the factory or pre-claim fallback. The family/mode atomic pair and effective Reduce motion/OS result arrive together before first paint. Offline/as-of readback stays truthful and never creates a write queue, last-painted hint or extra per-page reader.

heading_text: ERS-004 - Finding Classes And The Adjudicated Union

negative_constraints: - Do not let an adjudicator add a proposition to the union.
- Do not credit a finding without a cited passage stating the same proposition.
- Do not report unsupported-or-covered counts as a false-positive rate or as a model ranking.
owner_consumer: canonical_text: "Every research finding carries exactly one class: correction, a contradiction inside a promise the product already makes; capability, something the product does not yet do; product choice, a decision only the user can make; or unsupported_or_covered - in ordinary words, unsupported or already-covered - a proposal the product already owns or the evidence does not support. A topic's findings are adjudicated into one union, and a finding is credited to an arm only when a delivered assertion states the same proposition and cites the passage that supports it; a partial match is recorded as partial and never as a credit. A proposition outside the union is recorded as a candidate with its evidence, its classification and an explicit check against the expansions the union already rejected; adding a candidate to the union is the union owner's act, never the adjudicator's. unsupported_or_covered is a class of the union, not a false-positive rate."

heading_text: ERS-006 - Correction Landing Under Standing Repair Authorization

negative_constraints: - Do not land a correction without a currentness re-check against live canon.
- Do not accept a review by an agent that ran or scored any arm of the same topic.
- Do not land a correction that live canon already covers.
- Do not treat a static contract landing as runtime, security, performance or readiness evidence.
owner_consumer: canonical_text: "A finding classed correction lands without a new user decision, under the standing repair authorization, and only after three gates in order: a currentness re-check that re-reads every cited passage against live canon and re-adjudicates any passage that moved since the frozen snapshot; an independent review by an agent that ran no research job and scored no arm, whose verdict is recorded with the commit it reviewed; and a ledger that carries the correction, its evidence by path and SHA-256, and the owner PlanUnits it compiled to. A correction that a currentness re-check finds already covered is dropped with that reason recorded rather than landed. Where an obligation cannot be expressed in the contract surface, it lands as an owner obligation and the owner's validation_surfaces says so."
- Every landed correction names its evidence by path and SHA-256 and the owner PlanUnits it compiled to.

negative_constraints: - Do not declare a runtime version instead of reading the installed binary.
- Do not hash an output tree while a telemetry writer is still running.
- Do not record a freeze timestamp later than a job the freeze governed.

owner_consumer: canonical_text: "Every research run is reproducible from its own records. The run manifest pins the protocol freeze hash and the hash of every protocol file the run validated against, so two runs sharing a protocol fingerprint provably ran identical code, and the freeze timestamp must precede every job the freeze governed. The run's runtime identity - binary path, self-reported version and binary hash - is captured at capability time from the installed binary, never declared, and the boundary check compares the hash so a runtime that changes between gate and run fails closed. Every frozen output tree carries a SHA-256 output manifest, and the freeze procedure quiesces the monitor and every other telemetry writer before hashing, because a heartbeat written after the freeze makes an otherwise identical tree fail re-hashing. A re-hash difference is reported with the exact files that differ and whether any assertion document is among them."
- Runtime identity is read from the installed binary at capability time and compared at the boundary, failing closed on a mismatch.

The renderer availability order is Winit + Skia on the GPU (`winit-skia`), then Winit + Skia CPU raster (`winit-skia-software`). Runtime selection resolves in this order: `SLINT_BACKEND` explicit override, persisted renderer preference, Skia GPU default, then Skia CPU fallback. Slint itself falls back only when no GPU surface can be created, so Puppet Master also checks the GPU adapter at startup: when it is a software implementation (llvmpipe or lavapipe, WARP, SwiftShader), Puppet Master always uses Skia's CPU raster instead of running Skia on the software GPU, even when the Graphics Engine setting or the `SLINT_BACKEND` override asks for the GPU, and in that case it warns the user that no GPU was detected. When it switches to the CPU raster because of a software adapter, it shows one quiet, non-blocking, one-time notice explaining why frosted panels look solid, and never repeats it. The startup diagnostic records the requested and effective renderer and the reason. Apart from this software-adapter rule, explicit choices keep their precedence. FemtoVG and Slint's separate software renderer are not compiled; a `SLINT_BACKEND` value or persisted preference naming them is an unavailable backend that emits a startup diagnostic and falls through. `SLINT_BACKEND` remains valid for debugging, CI, and operator override, but persisted preferences must not silently override an explicit environment override. Startup diagnostics record the requested backend, effective backend, fallback reason, platform, GPU/driver summary when available, whether the fallback was operator-selected or automatic, and whether the Skia renderer extensions run in their GPU or CPU form.

heading_text: Migration, mandatory snapshot, and recovery shell

owner_consumer: - Preflight shows the storage-owner required-space formula, required bytes from `preflight_result.required_free_bytes`, and available bytes from `preflight_result.free_bytes`; insufficient space changes no target bytes.

- `applying` cannot begin until the shared-boundary backup is durable and verified. The version stamp commits only after migrated content verifies, and ordinary project chrome appears only after post-stamp verification; otherwise the journal drives verified restore/rollback or a blocked recovery state.

- A failure stays in the recovery shell and reports whether verified target, verified rollback, or neither is proven. Allowed actions are the owner-provided subset of retry recovery, update, choose compatible backup, metadata diagnostics, and quit. Retry reruns admission/recovery checks; it is not byte repair and never auto-resumes the blocked operation that encountered the failure.

The recovery shell exposes the mandatory verified-snapshot boundary without presenting JSON/JSONL export as a backup or an import path. A verified baseline is required before the first mutation-capable startup; additional mandatory snapshots cover the first dirty mutation within five minutes, a dirty store at 24 hours, and clean shutdown while dirty. The snapshot inspector shows verification state, shared-boundary/high-water ref, creation trigger, protected-reference/hold state, and the three-newest baseline policy. Amended 2026-10-31 (DL-270, BRS-031): the snapshot inspector, the restore confirmation and the recovery shell also show the last verified backup, meaning the newest backup at Structure verified or higher, with its verification level, its time and its last event, and what restoring from it would lose, in the existing `data_loss_risk.class` words with the boundary and family disclosure; a newer backup that has not verified is shown beside it, never instead of it. They add no second loss vocabulary and compute nothing themselves: all read the one backup-status record. Backup capture pauses writers only for a brief capture barrier, copying runs in the background without the writer lock, and derived families are not backed up and rebuild after a restore. If verification or restore fails, the GUI moves to viewer/recovery or blocked posture and discloses the last verified boundary, affected families, and maximum credible loss. It never calls canonical non-rebuildable state reconstructable merely because a projection can rebuild.

heading_text: Safe points, Assistant Chat restore points, and exact-replace outcomes

owner_consumer: | Concept | Canonical identity | User-visible meaning |

Creation is explicit through `cmd.chat.create_restore_point`; its confirmation names the inclusive source thread/branch/message boundary and records no workspace file bodies, secrets, stream state, or queue. Branching is only `cmd.chat.branch_from_restore`. Before dispatch, the surface shows the exact source boundary, whether that source is running or dirty, and that the target is a new conversation branch. Only owner result `branched` creates the new `thread_id` and `branch_id` and emits exactly one `restore_point.applied`; `refused` and `failed` return no target IDs and emit no application event. Replay returns the recorded result and same target IDs for `branched` without a duplicate event. A successful branch appends an application ref and does not consume the restore-point record. Every result and replay leaves the source thread, source conversation branch, source worktree, files, Git/index state, queue, and runtime safe points unchanged.

Restore-point lifecycle is exactly `available -> expired | deleted | corrupt`. Only `available` may expose the registered branch-from-restore action after permission, expected-record-hash, source-content, hold/ref, and storage-writer preflight. The effective policy shown is `RP-RESTOREPOINT-90D-AFTER-RELEASE@1.0.0`: eligibility is inclusive at owner-proven `reference_release + 7,776,000 seconds`, and count pressure at `2,048/project` selects only the oldest eligible record. Descendant branch/application refs, preserve/legal holds, in-flight application, source-lineage, live, recovery, backup, rollback, and maintenance refs override age and count eligibility until owner-defined release evidence is durable. The GUI shows policy/status but invents no expiry timer, release inference, undo window, hold clear, or new control. `cmd.chat.delete_restore_point` requires expected hash plus permission/storage preflight and remains disabled while any protecting ref exists; deletion never clears a hold.

Expired, deleted, corrupt, stale-hash, source-content-unavailable, permission-denied, viewer/blocked-storage, held-delete, and in-progress rows remain inspectable with their exact unavailable reason and no enabled mutation that violates the state. A deleted source thread stays hidden and is never resurrected: verified held boundary material may still create a visibly new branch, while unavailable deleted-source content returns `source_deleted_content_unavailable` and creates nothing. A `runtime_artifact.restore_point` is a projection of this Chat record; optional `safe_point_id` is lineage only and never changes its identity or grants file-restore semantics. Restore-point actions consume their current command-catalog rows and sole-handler production-wiring coverage; any live mismatch or unavailable owner family disables dispatch fail-closed.

`restored_with_conflicts` is invalid for safe-point restore and Chat revert. `cmd.chat.revert` resolves one immutable whole-turn mutation manifest; omitted `target_message_id` resolves once to the latest eligible mutating assistant turn, and no eligible turn returns `no_eligible_mutating_turn` without opening a restore transaction. Revert exact-replaces the whole affected-file scope, keeps transcript/queue/thread lifecycle unchanged, refreshes editors only after a durable owner result, and cannot report partial success. A removed target worktree is refused without recreating directories. Case L does not choose confirmation-versus-proceed UX for revert: the registered surface follows its existing command/permission policy while preserving the identical target and FileSafe guarantees. A `recovery_unavailable` episode remains blocked and anchored until explicit abandon, replan, or verified recovery. Buttons and menus dispatch only command-catalog-registered owner intents; this section does not mint `repair`, `salvage`, `import backup`, `force cancel`, `try anyway`, or estimated-completion actions.

Choosing the connect-existing path uses the exact bounded six-stage shortcut welcome -> simple_path -> remote_access_setup -> review_setup_plan -> automatic_preparation -> ready and does not fabricate empty first_project, source_control_setup, server_storage_client, provider_setup, or free_models_setup stages. Explicit Project Later follows PWIZ-037: set up paid-first AI and Free Models on the named Computer in application scope, then enter No project, without a placeholder Project or Settings copy. The bounded ten-theme choice appears at welcome before Project/infrastructure choices. It offers five ordered families, including NieR Light/Dark with Adjust NieR opening the same editor (F3-598); no independent checkbox remains (Q22). Before first paint in a claimed context, onboarding reads the saved Settings resolution for that exact Client/Computer and any real Project through SSYS-010/059/065, including the atomic general.visual.theme/general.visual.theme-mode pair, sound and effective Reduce motion with the OS preference. A valid saved look is preselected without a Basic Dark flash, even when no Project exists. Basic Dark is used only when no applicable saved look exists or as the ephemeral pre-claim fallback; opening onboarding never changes stored values. Run Onboarding Again (from Settings or the Home menu) retains the look then shown, NieR Mode included, preselected, without switching look as the window opens (DL-153 as qualified by DL-286). The window's hero moments take five styles, one per look family (F3-600). A persistent Look menu (`Change the look`), carrying the same five-family choices, one Light/Dark/Auto mode control that retains a prior Auto selection and follows system appearance live, and NieR Adjust button, and a sound control remain reachable in the onboarding header on every stage beyond welcome. The five families retain ten resolved Light/Dark appearances. Look selections preview presentation without dispatching owner work. Look and sound changes use SSYS-059/065’s classified target and exact writer. Claimed app scope may persist at an offered Everywhere/Computer/Device level without a Project; pre-claim preview is ephemeral. Project writes still require the real committed or connected Project. The ten-theme choice, Look menu and NieR Adjust editor use the existing typed local `ui.onboarding.choose_look` presentation and the Settings-owned classified binding; a durable choice calls the same Settings transaction, never cmd.theme.* or a private finish/close writer. Pre-claim preview remains ephemeral. The sound control consumes the Settings-owned `general.interaction.sound-effects` effective pref (or its bundled factory fallback while no applicable explicit level exists), stays keyboard-reachable with an explicit sound-off state, and audio is never the sole status signal; onboarding's cues are the onboarding and Guided Tour cue category of F3-599. In user language, the main journey welcomes the person, chooses whether to begin here or connect to an existing Puppet Master, drafts how to create or open their first project, chooses its safe version history, chooses the computer and storage places that will do and hold the work, offers private access, reviews the complete setup plan, prepares only the approved choices, and commits the approved Project once, offers paid-provider setup and then Free Models, and finishes in a concise Ready state. First Project choices persist a bounded uncreated draft, including a fresh-settings default or explicit Settings-owned copy preview. Before commit, only owner-authorized read-only preflight and just-in-time authentication necessary for the selected source are allowed by PWIZ-021; broad provider setup, enrollment, Connected Server pairing/trust, restore, repository creation or binding, filesystem writes, and Project creation are not. The sole pre-Review pairing exception is PWIZ-029's individually consented Server-owned selected-source access to a chosen folder, backup, or network storage on another Puppet Master: `cmd.client.pair.start` approval, code, or QR on the verified identity, recorded as `puppet_master` transport with a non-secret device-and-path reference and bound `source_access_authorization_refs`, limited to read-only browsing and validation of the chosen folder or backup under the current draft/session revision, hash, and expiry. The paired device stays a Source Location, backup source, or storage location and never becomes the Connected Server. Source sign-in uses the protected MACS-005 first-time variant when no verified account exists; it never invents a Project/account/repository identifier. Confirm and prepare validates the exact current draft/hash and PJCT-007 commit binding; Automatic Preparation observes the Project owner's one commit chain and any Settings-owned post-commit rebind/apply results. When a remote repository was created and a later step fails, Automatic Preparation keeps observing the same owner operation and shows the retained Project recovery with the three owner-routed choices Continue Setup, Open Repository, and Delete Repository; each choice stays disabled with its exact owner reason until its Project or Forge gates hold, an unknown remote effect offers reconciliation only, and no setup commit binding or provider phase advances until the listed persisted Project exists. Paid providers then use the actual committed Project, followed by Free Models after paid readiness or explicit Skip. Each screen has one clear decision, one dominant primary action, short human copy, automatic detection, safe defaults, and calm progressive disclosure. DL-259 H2/FF-20: the First Project decision shows three aligned, keyboard-reachable groups — New, Existing and Restore. Selecting Existing opens its local/online/device choices in the joined tray before sibling alternatives. The four semantic intents new/existing_local/existing_online/restore remain available; no unrelated More/Other disclosure hides a source route. Safe History is the beginner-facing local version timeline: Git and Jujutsu are equal available local history choices with no account; a fresh form may start with Git, existing inspected history wins, and submodules/LFS/hooks may explain a Git suggestion, FileSafe adds complementary local recovery points, and GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket, Forgejo or Gitea may hold a separate optional online copy without replacing local history. User-visible copy assumes no coding or IDE knowledge: it uses familiar words and never exposes the internal term `shell`, raw command/route/schema identifiers, owner names, host/environment vocabulary, provider matrices, diagnostics dashboards, network topology, or unexplained source-control jargon. Optional owner-routed branches cover opening an existing or online project, restoring a backup, keeping history locally or using a connected source service, discovering/pairing or manually locating another computer, setting up a work computer, optional service help, and private-access choices; advanced detail remains deferred or disclosed only when needed. Server, Storage, and this Client are three independent placements; local/mounted folders, advanced SSH/SFTP sources, and backup sources remain distinct. Every main stage has a scene-specific, theme-native cinematic composition rather than a generic repeated fade. The five theme families use substantially different illustration systems and directing language--Basic is an exact instructional blueprint, Friendly is an organic storybook workspace, Glass is a layered spatial composition, and Retro is a pixel/terminal sequence--rather than recoloring one shared image or silhouette. The fifth family, NieR, has its own system, including its onboarding preview: NieR ink marionettes in original line art and the NieR window touches of F3-598. The interruptible opening hero assembles the Puppet Master identity in approximately 1.2-1.5 seconds without blocking input; step transitions use 420-560 ms, element choreography uses 60-80 ms stagger, microinteractions use 120-220 ms, and success settles in approximately 700 ms. Reduced Motion preserves hierarchy with immediate state change or a very short opacity settle. Retro uses deliberate stepped, no-scale motion and hard compact reveals; Basic, Friendly, and Glass use material-appropriate easing and paint; NieR uses stepped, glow-free ink motion, and its hero moments, typed text and one-way large exits are F3-598's. Those moments do not hold input. A resumed onboarding repaints the session's stored look_choice, NieR Mode included, with null fields falling back to this unit's start rule (DL-153). Amended 2026-10-17 (DL-228): in every look the application beneath stays still while the window is open: nothing in it animates, takes focus or wakes until both the window and its exit have finished. After O12’s owner-completion and last-block gates hold, Ready’s Enter answers on the click’s frame. The actual destination selected by PWIZ-021/PWIZ-037 is drawn whole beneath the window: the Planning Wizard for its committed Project path, the No project chat for Set up a project later (including Skip AI), or the owner-selected connected destination for connect-existing. The window’s exit is the only move, and the hand-over never passes through Home; no Project workflow is synthesized for Later. F3-598 consumes this rule. The Home options menu row is named Run Onboarding Again everywhere (DL-153, UCC-200); Run setup wizard is its earlier name, and it sits directly below Restore home layout, the former Reset Layout. Amended 2026-10-29 (O1–O12; PM7): F3-663 supersedes the troupe, no-physics/no-loop prohibition and separately drawn spinner. One Pip in distinct family worlds, bounded shared life and solved strings, with implementation technique open under Jared’s O2 A ruling of 2026-10-30, six kits including Retro split, live voice/music through one player. One option-anchored ? opens the shared explanatory note (DL-260). All real routes/errors/203 tips expand beyond the small concept. O12 B (Jared 2026-10-30) amends the former animation-never-gates rule: Creating Continue and Ready wait for owner completion and the last block to land; Reduced Motion settles instantly. Real flow and 14 onboarding actions remain. O11 defers the Tour. O7 (2026-10-29): preserving the settled scene during Details/? permits F3-663’s same-stage choice preview, note-directed Pip and typed answer/idea cue; no choice commit or entrance replay. The older settled-scene acceptance is read with this specific interaction. O6, Jared 2026-10-30: hovering a look tile changes neither the theme nor sound. Click or keyboard activation requests ui.onboarding.choose_look; this keeps the existing ephemeral/current-Project persistence boundary. Amended Q22, Jared 2026-10-30 (DL-257): the fifth NieR family supersedes independent-override wording; SSYS-043 owns migration and retained Adjust controls. Q22 visible copy is Adjust NieR, or Adjust NieR… in the title-bar menu (foundations source confirmation 1030182542-5544). The earlier label Adjust NieR look is retained as historical source text only. QA round 2, Jared 2026-10-30; DL-258; GUI 7d586bad18: Q6/Q7: point to the actual backup before asking to unlock it. A Recovery Kit is an untrusted locator plus protected recovery credential, not a storage place, backup payload, NAS password or cloud sign-in. Offer the Kit first, then the explicit no-Kit path to a folder, another device/NAS, or a cloud service. Continue waits for the selected file/folder/device/account and required fields. Validate the locator/trust and reach/authenticate the selected place through its existing owner. An accepted Kit may unlock that backup, but cannot bypass storage authentication. Show Unlock the backup only for a still-locked backup without an accepted unlock; name its selected place. Select a copy, coverage and preview only afterwards. Repointing invalidates the former unlock and snapshot selection. Owner recovery prerequisites, approval, protected secret handling and actual restore/Project commit boundaries remain mandatory; only a verified Backup owner result proves unlock or restore. Q7/H2/H8: a selected choice’s follow-up belongs immediately in a tray joined to that card, before sibling alternatives. One shared joined-choice component owns the join, indentation and line from the parent mark across all twelve affected screens (DL-258; source mechanics stay lineage under DL-260). The parent opens into the tray in every look, with matching edges, no gap or overlapping lower corner/ring; narrow layouts put the parent question note first inside the tray. Arrow keys stay in their own choice list, and the option, its radio and question control never overlap. Apply to backup places/Kit, existing-work origins, work computer checks, sign-up links, Settings copy, remote route and proxy-configuration choices (certificate choices removed by CERT-1 / srv C1), online service kind/address, device notes and connection routes. Naming and Review display the same selected mounted/network source, rather than an empty local-location field. Q3/Q8/Q9: question controls answer pointer hover and keyboard focus in the current look. Remove duplicate explanation-only disclosures (What is a Server?, the Connect proxy explanation, and What does Puppet Master read? on Choose a key); put their information in the shared option tips. Keep functional sections: More about keeping versions contains FileSafe, Which proxy contains the Caddy/NGINX/Traefik selector; identity fingerprints and Creating/restore receipts are data and remain. H3: SMB sign-in uses the operating system’s shared-folder keychain; Puppet Master stores no password. The SSH add-key password remains a separate one-use protected flow; never reuse its never-saved hint for SMB. H5: the onboarding owner holds one original inert-state basis for the entire open lifetime. Replacing an already-open screen acquires only newly encountered background nodes; it never re-snapshots nodes already held by that modal as originally inert. Every close/finish/skip path removes only the modal’s own holds, preserves pre-existing inert nodes and restores focus/input. Q1/Q2: onboarding sound defaults on under general.interaction.sound-effects, through the existing one player and trusted-gesture gate. Until the Settings owner supplies the applicable sound preference, retain the factory-on or current effective choice rather than muting on every refresh. An explicit readable Project value wins when it binds; a genuinely refused bound write remains refused. An unavailable Settings projection never fabricates a saved value or authorizes a write. QA2 follow-up N1, integration 6609384fd0; DL-258: A reached backup place is bound to the selected service or device, not a reusable signed-in/ready boolean. Choosing another source, service, device, Kit or folder invalidates its old reach proof, protected access fields, unlock, copy selection and completed bucket check. A late sign-in/check result stays bound to the service/device it authenticated and cannot advance a different current choice. A protected SSH key passphrase unlock belongs to that exact selected key; changing keys requires that key’s own owner-proven access and never inherits another key’s unlock. The Remote Link endpoint belongs only to the Remote Link route; choosing Only at home/local-or-VPN, Tailscale or another route clears it from the reviewed draft. No stale endpoint enters an unrelated route. DL-259, Jared 2026-10-31: D1 A: the online-service step creates or selects a code repository; onboarding does not publish a website, GitHub Pages, GitLab Pages or another site. Local-only Project choices remain valid. D2 A: explicit always-on Server setup on this computer, manual private HTTPS, a self-hosted Remote Link gateway, rarer SSH key types, China-region AI variants and local AI servers live in Settings, with a clear context-correct pointer from onboarding. The ordinary This computer choice remains the easy local-work default. The wizard says AI accounts available in this setup, not every AI. Existing Settings routes and owners retain the advanced capabilities. D3 A: generated proxy settings support Caddy, NGINX and Traefik, with Caddy the default. Nginx Proxy Manager is existing-only: it can be selected as an existing proxy but never sent to a generation/install/export operation. DL-259 CERT-1 / srv C1, Jared 2026-10-31: onboarding offers Make the settings file or I have one already. The first generates/exports Caddy, NGINX or Traefik configuration for the person to add on their own system before the owner’s DNS, reachability and live-connection checks; Caddy is the default. The second only checks the existing proxy route and live connection, with nothing generated. Set it up for me is removed: Puppet Master does not install or host the proxy. The onboarding draft carries proxy_hosting=generate_only or existing_proxy for this new-Server proxy branch and keeps proxy_tls null; it collects no certificate choice. Generating a file proves neither installation nor consent, identity, secure reachability or a live route. For generation, onboarding proxy_kind is exactly caddy, nginx or traefik and maps to reverse_proxy_configuration.proxy_family. The existing-proxy branch may record nginx_proxy_manager but never emits a generated-configuration record; neither branch silently substitutes a family. D4: confirm provider admission and executable conformance immediately before building Puppet Master. The wizard lists its provider choices without unconfirmed/not-verified badges, warnings or caveats. This scheduling decision does not change per-account authentication, entitlement, health or quota truth: Ready is the shared account owner’s current usable result, not merely signed in. D6 A: the human signs in on the initiating active device while the AI/tool runs on the selected execution host. Official tool sign-ins and private account roots stay with that tool on that host; direct API keys are held by Puppet Master’s secure credential store on that host. Onboarding, Settings, model selection and Usage share stable account/profile/host/environment references, never provider-name booleans or copied secrets. Protected returns are bound to the exact operation, initiating Client/session/generation and execution host. Changing account, host or route invalidates stale validation; another account of the same provider has a distinct identity. D7 B supersedes the former no-per-Client-node restriction. Native Puppet Master apps on Windows, macOS and Linux have their own built-in Tailscale connection and sign in once through the shared protected auth owner, with no separate Tailscale app install. The same signed PM-owned Go tsnet helper is supervised by its owning PM process. A Server keeps one active node per stable server_id; a native Client installation keeps one active node per stable client_id, independent of Projects, windows, tabs, sessions and Server endpoint selection. Owner-qualified configuration, process, IPC, authorization, egress and secure-state references prevent identity/key sharing or duplicate active nodes. Native Client nodes provide bounded Dial/stream access only to verified PM endpoints, not arbitrary proxying or a Server public listener. Server nodes retain the automatic private listener; Funnel remains Server-only, explicit, off by default and unavailable on Headscale. Human approval and reusable connection identity do not grant PM pairing/trust or work permission. A plain browser tab has no embedded Tailscale connection: it needs Remote Link or a private endpoint reachable through the device’s own Tailscale connection. It cannot be enrolled by a browser sign-in. Existing user-managed host Tailscale stays external and unmanaged. D8 A: onboarding has one FileSafe switch, default on, covering command blocklist, write scope, security filter and pre-write safe points together. Individual controls remain in Settings. The switch expresses a requested owner configuration, never approval to bypass a required guard, an absent allowlist/baseline, failed canonical-path resolution, failed initialization or failed safe-point persistence. Mandatory policy and effective guard state win; a refused change stays refused with a clear reason. No failure silently turns a guard off. ELI5: the wizard bar and Guided Tour bar expose the same global general.interaction.mode through the Settings owner, with values ELI5 and Expert, labels Plain English and Expert, and default ELI5. Both bars reflect the same effective state. Every opened onboarding question tip and prose help section has useful Plain English and technical versions, including FileSafe, service differences, storage, remote access and AI/auth choices, assuming no coding experience. Screen copy, control labels, exact fingerprints, paths and receipt data stay single; dual copy is limited to tips/help (DL-126). A mode change updates an open tip without rewriting a chat reply. Existing cmd.settings.transaction.preview/apply owns the preference; ui.guided_tour.toggle_eli5 is a compatibility local adapter to that shared preference, not a tour-only setting or chat ELI5 command. The predecessor tour_narration_only tag is retired. DL-257/Q22 and DL-259 QA2 M4, 2026-10-31: the welcome look chooser gives Basic, Friendly, Glass, Retro and NieR equal choice prominence. Each tile has an accessible family label and reachable question/Adjust controls where applicable. At narrow and short supported sizes the title, all five choices and footer remain readable and reachable without clipping or a hidden extra-family strip; the chooser fits above the footer or scrolls within its bounded content area. Click or keyboard activation selects; silent hover does not select. DL-259 late integration, 2026-10-31: for an unnamed Project using the automatic local destination, Name shows the base destination plus “in a folder with your Project’s name”. The line inserts the selected Computer’s resolved code.execution.projects-folder destination. Its factory value is execution_host_home_relative Projects, expanded against that actual Host’s home (for example ~/Projects on Unix), never a fixed Documents destination or the initiating Client’s home. A placeholder or unselected suggestion never supplies a chosen folder leaf. Typing a name or explicitly choosing a suggestion adds that current draft name; clearing it restores the generic line. The local-location picker’s On this computer card names the base destination. Existing folders and selected network/mounted/remote sources still display their actual resolved location under H8. These are truthful draft previews and create no folder or Project before the reviewed commit. DL-259 late integration, 2026-10-31: pressing the AI phase’s Skip for now immediately acknowledges the skipped choice and brings its concise skipped-state/consequence message into view at the start of that step, rather than leaving the feedback below a long provider list. It does not wait for detection, sign-in or key checks. Optional Free Models remains available and continuation reflects the explicit phase skip. No account becomes Ready from skipping; current paid/free account usability still comes from its owner. This phase skip remains distinct from whole-session Skip. Reduced Motion reveals the feedback in its settled position. DL-259 FO-4, 2026-10-31: onboarding provider rows and connected-account summaries show the category and concise product/account identity without billing explanations, prices, limits or extra-usage pitches. Retain useful category names and exact account/product distinctions; this presentation rule does not alter the provider owner’s charging model, auth surface, account identity or credential custody. DL-259 FO-6, 2026-10-31: a protected field keeps its typed value through redraws of the same screen and field identity, including typing in another field, opening help and changing Plain English/Expert. A blank rendering template alone must not erase it. The action clears the field when it consumes the input; leaving/recreating the screen, changing its service/method/target or explicit cancel/reset clears it too. Keep that input only in the protected entry control until consumption, never in ordinary draft/session persistence, receipts or logs. A filled/masked flag is not a credential or validation proof; submission reads the current protected value and rechecks its existing owner requirements. DL-259 FO-9 final, 2026-10-31: Creating’s checklist and block stack share the accepted owner’s phase/effect projection. When GitHub creation only partly settles, show only verified completed phases as checked or landed blocks; the phase proven to have failed may show failure and unexecuted/unproven phases remain pending. Unexecuted or unproven phases stay pending through an incomplete or unclear result until a later accepted owner result from Continue Setup or Check again proves those effects settled. The checklist, stage block count and stage progress use that same result; a settled phase keeps its block and an unproven phase has no completed block. Refresh alone neither completes a phase nor repeats a settled remote create. Transport completion and animation never prove the later registration, settings or connection steps. The recovery banner/actions, Continue availability and Ready use that same current owner result; O12’s last-block landing condition is additional to owner completion, never a replacement for it. DL-259 FO-10 final, 2026-10-31: on Connect’s route screen, disabled Continue gives an actionable reason for the selected route’s visible input before an unresolved Server-choice reason. Web address and Remote Link use that field’s current missing/invalid-address result; an address typed instead of the found list asks for the address when empty and explains when no Puppet Master answers, with a route back to the list. Say Choose your Puppet Master only while the found-Server choice list is shown. Pip’s feedback conveys the same cause. These screen/status words stay single in Plain English and Expert (DL-126); only tips/help have two versions. Reason priority changes no validation, route identity, readiness, pairing or permission gate and admits no address/Remote Link grammar. DL-271 FO-11, 2026-10-31: where an OpenCode server requires its own HTTP Basic credentials, the Password field asks for that server’s password, not an AI provider’s API key or the person’s Puppet Master sign-in. Its hint states that distinction and identifies credential custody in the OS keychain on the selected execution host, through the existing credential owner. Optional server auth stays optional when the server needs none. Protected entry, secret-free readback and exact host/account binding remain; an API-key-only hint is used only on an actual API-key field. DL-271 FO-12, 2026-10-31: Protect’s missing-access guidance is count-neutral: ask for the access details without claiming a fixed number of fields. The selected Backup destination family, auth method and credential mode determine the actual required fields and validation through their existing owner. Changing the line never omits a required credential, locator, region or temporary-session value and never turns incomplete access into an available Connect action. DL-271 Unlock wording, 2026-10-31: ask for your recovery phrase, rather than six words or another fixed word count. The Recovery Kit is not a six-word format (PWIZ-025/BRS-018); the Backup owner still defines and verifies the real protected recovery material and its exact source/target binding. The wording admits no new phrase format, key derivation, unlock proof or weaker secret-handling rule. DL-271 weak-key eligibility, 2026-10-31: Choose a key may list a DSA or RSA-1024 key as Too weak to use, but it cannot be selected, used as a default, advanced or installed. The refusal reads Older key type — too weak to use. Check this eligibility before an existing authorization, matching prior profile or passphrase/unlock state; those cannot make a weak key usable. A retained weak selection must be replaced by an owner-eligible key before the flow advances. Other keys keep their existing owner checks, identity binding and custody; the shared list never exposes or moves a private half. DL-271 initial request waiting, 2026-10-31: while the current invitation is live and no device request has arrived, Your Server is ready shows No requests yet with Check again. Checking re-reads the current owner run; a real arriving request also updates that view. This neutral state is not an error and invents no candidate, approval or trust. Continue retains its existing Server-ready gates. Keep it distinct from DL-259 FO-7’s answered approval/rejection: a completed request stays answered, and a fresh request requires the existing new-code/new-generation route.

compatibility_only: Guided Tour teaches through successful actions over the mounted Puppet Master application in one stable chapter order: Assistant Chat with Teacher, workspace practice, then Planning Wizard. Chat opens through its real control; the learner sends the supplied local question, sees Teacher's answer stream in the same labeled guided-example conversation, and then sees that same answer in simple words through Explain this reply simply (`cmd.chat.eli5.explain_reply`), which adds one extra, simpler reply after the example answer and never rewrites or regenerates the original; the callout then points to the quick dot by the message box, which makes later replies simple, and names the ELI5 popup behind the wand's ELI5 row (the ELI5 sheet, F3-581), where the chat's choice is set (DL-126, ACD-484). Workspace practice explains navigation and panels and follows the workspace chapter named in the 2026-10-09 amendment below (PWIZ-035). Every important action offers Try it and Show Me; both invoke the same mounted owner handler and satisfy the same observed success predicate. Show Me uses interruptible pre-cue, visible travel, destination reaction, and settle, never teleportation or a second implementation. Planning Wizard is about half of meaningful actions and dwell time. Amended 2026-10-17 (DL-230, Jared): the bar is that Planning is about half of the tour's actions and time (it read: at least half); the accepted 20-step tour, Planning at 44 percent of actions and 49 percent of dwell, meets it. Jared will redo the tour completely once chat is rolled in and the Planning Wizard is redesigned, so no other tour work is planned until then. A book-club goal becomes three outcomes, the learner answers who may edit, sees why it matters, reviews decisions/assumptions/ unresolved choices, edits one answer, and watches only the affected shared-access consequence change before the approval boundary. Teacher retains a broad discoverable beginner question library. The shared Plain English / Expert control remains beside Pause and Skip and is called out in the first scene; the same opening moment explains that people who prefer less animation can enable Reduced Motion later in Settings. All visible copy is written for a person who has never coded or used an IDE and never calls the application a `shell` or exposes command IDs, owners, providers, models, tokens, receipts, routes, or implementation terms. The overlay tracks and highlights mounted controls without cloning them, intercepting owner work, or fabricating success. Automatic scene transitions focus the current scene heading, never an action, and do not open a visual hover tag without user intent. Pause, Back, Skip, interruption, resize, theme change, and effective Reduced Motion preserve real state and focus. The Tour bar carries the same persistent Look menu (`Change the look`) and sound control beyond setup on every step: Look choices, family nier and its Adjust NieR editor included (F3-598), apply through the Settings owner at the exact offered level, and the Tour follows the effective look for its actual app or Project context. Neither control is a `ui.guided_tour.*` action (DL-153): a family/mode Look choice or live edit in the editor and the sound control's write of `general.interaction.sound-effects` compose cmd.settings.transaction.preview then cmd.settings.transaction.apply, and Adjust NieR is ui.settings.nier_editor.open. Both are shared chrome controls, not tour-specific preference toggles, and audio is never the sole status signal; the Tour's cues are the onboarding and Guided Tour cue category of F3-599. Back and forward movement follow the valid story state and never become inert or skip required practice. Basic, Friendly, Glass, Retro and NieR (F3-598), direct the film with substantially different callout composition, illustration, typography, target treatment, and motion--not one recolored overlay--while never using a left-edge accent rail.
